statement.name: Π01-generic approximation principle
statement.definition: For any uniformly Π01 collection of dense sets of strings D_i there is a sequence g_0,g_1,... of reals with (∀i)(∃m)(∃t)(∀u>t)[g_u↾m = g_t↾m ∈ D_i].
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 + IΣ02 (Thm 3.2); RCA0 + BΣ02 + Π01GA proves IΣ02 (Thm 3.3); implied by Π01G, hence Π11-conservative over RCA0 and does not imply BΣ02; AMT does not imply it (Cor. 3.4). It is the key principle in Figure 2 for entries marked 3 and 4.

statement.name: Π0n generic approximation (and Π0nG)
statement.definition: Approximations in the sense of the iterated limit lemma to generics for uniformly Π0n sequences of dense sets of strings.
statement.facts: RCA0 + IΣ0n+1 proves Π0nGA (Thm A.1); RCA0 + BΣ0n+1 + Π0nGA proves IΣ0n+1 (Thm A.2); Π0nG is Π11-conservative (indeed restricted Π12-conservative) over RCA0.

statement.name: Atomic Tree Theorem
statement.definition: If T is an atomic extendible tree, then there is a listing of the isolated paths of T.
statement.facts: ATT implies AMT; provable from Π01G and from RCA0 + BΣ02 + AMT; restricted Π12-conservative over RCA0 and Π11-conservative over RCA0 + BΣ02. Open whether AMT implies ATT.

statement.name: Finite Atomic Tree Theorem
statement.definition: For an atomic extendible tree and finitely many nodes there are isolated paths extending each of them.
statement.facts: Follows from BΣ02 and from ATT; not provable in RCA0 (Thm B.2). Open whether Π01GA implies it.

statement.name: ATT with strengthened hypothesis
statement.definition: An extendible tree satisfying the conclusion of FATT has a listing of its isolated paths.
statement.facts: Intermediate between ATT and AMT; no results proved.

statement.name: Homogeneous Model Theorem
statement.definition: For a theory T and a list X of types satisfying the finite full amalgamation closure conditions there is a homogeneous model A with T(A) = X.
statement.facts: Equivalent to AMT over RCA0 (Thm 7.6) and uniformly (Weihrauch) equivalent to AMT (Thm 7.11); HMT-bounding degrees coincide with AMT-bounding degrees (Cor. 7.12).

statement.name: Weak Model Existence Theorem
statement.definition: For a theory T and a list X of types satisfying the finite free amalgamation closure conditions there is a model A with T(A) = X.
statement.facts: Equivalent to AMT over RCA0 (Thm 7.6); uniformly equivalent to AMT (Thm 7.11).

statement.name: 1-Point Homogeneous Model Theorem
statement.definition: Analogue of HMT with 1-point full amalgamation closure conditions and 1-point homogeneous models.
statement.facts: Equivalent to AMT + IΣ02 over RCA0 (Thm 7.7).

statement.name: 1-Homogeneous Model Theorem; Strong Model Existence Theorem
statement.definition: HMT-style statements with pairwise full amalgamation (1-homogeneous models), resp. pairwise free amalgamation (arbitrary models).
statement.facts: Each implies AMT over RCA0 (Thm 7.8); provable in RCA0 + ATT + Π01GA (Thm 7.9); not provable in RCA0 + ATT + BΣ02 (Thm 7.10); exact strength open.

statement.name: Extension function approximation existence under closure conditions C
statement.definition: Every list of types satisfying closure conditions C has an extension function approximation.
statement.facts: For finite full or finite free amalgamation, equivalent to AMT over RCA0; for pairwise full, pairwise free or 1-point full, implies AMT and is implied by ATT (Thm 7.5).

statement.name: Jullien's theorem (essential segment formulation)
statement.definition: A scattered linear ordering is extendible iff it has no essential segment of the form 2 or R+Q with R indecomposable to the right and Q indecomposable to the left.
statement.facts: The left-to-right direction is provable in RCA0. JUL implies FRA over RCA0. FRA plus Σ¹₁-IND implies JUL; JUL and FRA are equivalent over RCA0 + Σ¹₁-IND.

statement.name: Signed trees are well quasi-ordered
statement.definition: Every sequence of well-founded {+,-}-labelled trees has i<j with a homomorphism from T_i to T_j.
statement.facts: Equivalent to FRA and FINDEC over RCA0 (Theorem 4.2, Corollary 3.7). Implies ATR0 over RCA0 (Proposition 2.14). Follows from FRA.

statement.name: Finite decomposability of scattered linear orderings
statement.definition: Every scattered linear ordering is equimorphic to a finite sum of h-indecomposable linear orderings.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to WQO(ST) and FRA, and to the existence of minimal decompositions of scattered linear orderings (Corollary 3.11). Implies ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Jullien's theorem via minimal decompositions
statement.definition: For a minimal decomposition F_0..F_n of L, L is extendible iff no F_i=F_{i+1}=1 and no F_i indecomposable to the right followed by F_{i+1} indecomposable to the left.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR* (ATR0 + Σ¹₁-IND) over RCA0 + Σ¹₁-IND (Theorem 5.14). The left-to-right direction is provable in RCA0.

statement.notation: extendibility of ω*, ζ, η, ω^2, h-indecomposables
statement.name: Extendibility of linear orderings
statement.definition: A linear ordering L is extendible if every countable partial ordering not embedding L has a linearization not embedding L.
statement.facts: ATR* proves extendibility of ω*, (ω²)*, η and every h-indecomposable linear ordering (Theorems 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.20), with hyperarithmetic linearizations. Extendibility of ζ implies ATR0 (cited DHLS03).

statement.name: First-order (recursive) version of RT^2_2
statement.definition: For any X and c : [N]^2 → 2, if IΣ^X_1 fails, then there is an index of a Δ^X_1 set which is infinite and homogeneous for c.
statement.facts: RCA0* + RT^2_2 proves it. Over RCA0* + ¬IΣ^0_1 it is equivalent to RT^2_2, so RT^2_2 is equivalent to a Π^1_1 statement there. It is not provable in RCA0*, even in its lightface version.

statement.name: First-jump control statement for RT^2_2
statement.definition: For any sets X, Z with X′ ≪ Z′ and any coloring c : [N]^2 → 2 with c ≤_T X, there is an index of a Σ^Z_2 set H which is infinite homogeneous for c and satisfies (X ⊕ H)′ ≪ Z′.
statement.facts: RCA0 + IΣ^0_2 proves it (Theorem 5). RCA0 + RT^2_2 proves it (Theorem 14). Whether RCA0 + BΣ^0_2 proves it is open; RT^2_2 is Π^1_1-conservative over RCA0 + BΣ^0_2 if and only if RCA0 + BΣ^0_2 proves it (Corollary 7). It can be formulated as a Π^0_5 statement.

statement.name: Bounded enumeration scheme
statement.definition: A scheme of sentences from Chong–Slaman–Yang [7], now known to be equivalent to the well-orderedness of ω, ω^ω, ….
statement.facts: RCA0 + RT^2_2 + BME is a Π^0_4-conservative extension of RCA0 + BΣ^0_2 + BME (Theorem 10).

statement.name: Determinacy of win/lose games with Γ winning set (Nash equilibria of two-player games), Cantor space
statement.definition: Takes a two-player win/lose game on {0,1}^N whose winning set for player 1 is in Γ and returns a Nash equilibrium, i.e. a pair of strategies one of which is winning. Differs from catalogue det-sigma, which is on Baire space.
statement.facts: Det_A ≡W FindWS_A ≡W C_{0,1}^N for closed sets A (Theorem 9). Det_{D_{n+1}} ≡W C_{0,1}^N⋆lim^(n)-type degree: Det_{D_{n+1}} ≡W (C_{0,1}^N)^[n] (Theorem 15), and Det_D ≡W C_{0,1}^N ⋆ lim for D the differences of closed sets (introduction). Det_D is equivalent to the Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem by combining with [10]. Det_Γ ≡W Det of the complement class.

statement.name: Deciding the winner of Γ win/lose games
statement.definition: Same inputs as Det_Γ; decides which player (if any) has a winning strategy.
statement.facts: Win_A ≡W LPO (Proposition 10). Win_{D_{n+1}} ≡W LPO^[n] (Theorem 15). Win_{D(Γ)} ≤W LPO ⋆s Win^_Γ (Lemma 11).

statement.name: Finding winning strategies for Γ games (Cantor space)
statement.definition: Restriction of Det_Γ to games in which the first player has a winning strategy.
statement.facts: FindWS_A ≡W Det_A ≡W C_{0,1}^N (Theorem 9). FindWS_Γ ≡W its parallelization for pointclasses closed under a countable-union operation (Proposition 20).

statement.name: Nash equilibria of sequential games with finitely/countably many outcomes
statement.definition: Operations taking sequential games with countably many players and Γ-measurable outcome sets to Nash equilibria. NE^ap restricts to two players with antagonistic preferences.
statement.facts: NE^ap_Γ ≤W Det*_Γ × Win*_Γ (Theorem 21). NE_Γ ≤W Win^_Γ × Det^_Γ (Theorem 22). NE^ap_{O∪A} ≡W C_{0,1}^N × LPO* (Theorem 29). NE^ap_{D_{n+1}∪D_{n+1}} ≡W C_{0,1}^N^[n] × (LPO^[n])* (Theorem 30). C_{0,1}^N × LPO* ≤W NE_{O∪A} ≤W lim (Corollary 32).

statement.name: Subgame-perfect equilibria of antagonistic games
statement.definition: Takes a two-player game with finitely many outcomes and antagonistic preferences and returns a subgame-perfect equilibrium.
statement.facts: SPE_Γ ≤W Win^_Γ × Det^_Γ (Theorem 23). SPE_{O∪A} ≡W lim, and more generally SPE_{D_n∪D_n} ≡W lim^(n) (Theorem 31). Win^_{Γ1} ≤W SPE_Γ under the hypotheses of Lemma 28.

statement.name: Arithmetical levels of LLPO and LEM
statement.definition: Σ^0_n-LLPO takes a pair (p0,p1) of sequences and outputs i such that the Σ^0_n statement for p_i holds. Σ^0_n-LEM decides the truth of a Σ^0_n statement.
statement.facts: Σ^0_{n+1}-LLPO ≡W LLPO^[n] and Σ^0_{n+1}-LEM ≡W LPO^[n] (Proposition 13). Σ^0_n-LEM ≤W Win_{D_n} and the parallelization of Σ^0_n-LLPO ≤W Det_{D_n} (Lemma 14).

statement.name: Σ11-choice principle on X (e.g. Σ11-C_N, Σ11-C_{N^N})
statement.definition: Given a code of a nonempty analytic subset of X, choose an element of it.
statement.facts: Σ11-C_{N^N} ≡W C_{N^N} (Proposition 2.2, with the reduction Σ11-C_{N^N} ≤W C_{N^N}). The parallelization of Σ11-C_2 is equivalent to Σ11-WKL and Π11-Sep. The parallelization of Σ11-C_N is equivalent to Σ11-KC, ATR2′ (arithmetically) and Π11-Tot2 (Corollary 2.9 and Theorem 2.10).

statement.name: Σ11 axiom of choice, restricted variants
statement.definition: Parallelization of Σ11-choice. The restrictions are fin, cof, foc, aof and aou (finite, cofinite, finite-or-cofinite, all-or-finite, all-or-unique), plus fosc (finite-or-strongly-cofinite).
statement.facts: Σ11-AC^fin ≡W Σ11-DC^fin <W Σ11-AC^aof ≡W Σ11-DC^aof ≡W Σ11-AC^aou ≡W Σ11-AC^fosc (Theorem 3.37, Corollaries 3.12 and 3.14). Σ11-AC^cof is Weihrauch incomparable with Σ11-AC^fin and Σ11-AC^aof (Corollary 3.23). Σ11-AC^aof and Σ11-AC^cof are not reducible to Σ11-KσC (Corollaries 3.19 and 3.26). Σ11-AC_{N^N} <W Σ11-DC_{N^N} (Theorem 3.34). Upward density of the Medvedev lattices of Σ11-AC^cof, Σ11-AC^foc and Σ11-AC_{N^N} (Theorems 3.24, 3.27, 3.29).

statement.name: Σ11 dependent choice
statement.definition: Given a Σ11 set Y and a Σ11 relation satisfying the premise of dependent choice, return a sequence f with f(0) = a0 and R(f(n), f(n+1)) for all n.
statement.facts: C_{N^N} ≡W [Σ11-DC_{N^N}]mv ≡W [Σ11-DC_N]mv (Proposition 2.2). Σ11-DC_{N^N} ≡W Σ11-AC^fin ⋆ Σ11-AC^cof (Theorem 3.34). Σ11-AC ⋆ Σ11-AC ≡W Σ11-AC ⋆ Σ11-AC ⋆ Σ11-AC, so compositional powers stabilize at level two.

statement.name: Compact and σ-compact Σ11 choice
statement.definition: Σ11-choice restricted to compact Σ11 sets. The σ-compact version takes a sequence of compact Σ11 sets, at least one nonempty.
statement.facts: Σ11-KC ≡W Σ11-WKL ≡W the parallelization of Σ11-C_2 (Proposition 2.5, Fact 2.4). Σ11-KσC is not parallelizable, and Σ11-KC <W Σ11-KσC (Corollary 3.20).

statement.name: Totalization and diagonalization for partial Π11 functions
statement.definition: Given a partial Π11 function into 2 (or ω), find a total extension. DNC: given a sequence of partial Π11 functions, find a total function diagonalizing against it.
statement.facts: The parallelization of Σ11-C_2 ≡W Π11-Tot2 ≡W Π11-DNC2 (Proposition 2.6). The parallelization of Σ11-C^aou_N ≡W Π11-TotN (Proposition 2.7). Π11-DNCN ≤W Π11-DNC2 ≤W Π11-TotN.

statement.name: Variants of two-sided ATR
statement.definition: ATR2′: given a linear order, return a jump hierarchy on a large initial segment (one containing the well-founded part) or an infinite descending sequence. ATR2^po: the same as ATR2 for partial orders.
statement.facts: The parallelization of ATR2′ is arithmetically Weihrauch equivalent to Σ11-KC and to the parallelization of Σ11-C^aou_N (Theorem 2.10). Σ11-C^aou_N ≤W ATR2^po (Proposition 2.13). ATR ≤W ATR2′ ≤W ATR2 ≤W ATR2^po ≤W Σ11-C_{N^N}. Whether ATR2, ATR2′ and ATR2^po are arithmetically equivalent is open (Question 2.14).

statement.name: Totalization of Σ11 unique choice
statement.definition: Σ11-choice restricted to singletons, extended to a total problem: any value is accepted if the set is not a singleton.
statement.facts: Σ11-UC^tot_X ≡W Σ11-C^aou_X for X a Δ11 subset of N (Proposition 2.8). The parallelization of Σ11-UC^tot_2 ≡W Σ11-KC_{N^N} (Corollary 2.9).

statement.name: Existence of upward closures in posets
statement.definition: For every subset Q of a poset P, the upward closure of Q exists as a set.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA₀ over RCA₀.

statement.notation: Analytic-Regularity (all analytic sets A ⊂ [0,1] are Lebesgue-regular)
statement.name: Lebesgue-regularity of analytic sets
statement.definition: Every analytic set A ⊂ [0,1] has equal outer and inner Lebesgue measure, where outer measure is the infimum of λ(B) over open B ⊇ A and inner measure is the supremum of λ(B) over compact B ⊆ A.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Σ¹₁-Induction over ATR₀ (Theorem 1); the reversal is Lemma 6 over ACA₀. Σ¹₁-IND with ATR₀ also gives regularity of all analytic sets A ⊂ R (Theorem 33).

statement.notation: Analytic-Measurability (all analytic sets A ⊂ [0,1] are Lebesgue-measurable)
statement.name: Lebesgue-measurability of analytic sets
statement.definition: Every analytic set A ⊂ [0,1] is Lebesgue-regular and the common value λ(A) exists as a real number.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π¹₁-CA₀ over ATR₀ (Theorem 2); the reversal is Lemma 7 over ACA₀. Π¹₁-CA₀ gives measurability of all analytic A ⊂ R (Theorem 34).

statement.name: Σ¹₁-Induction
statement.definition: The induction scheme for Σ¹₁ formulas (with set parameters), for natural numbers.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA₀ to finite Σ¹₁-Comprehension (Lemma 5). Equivalent to regularity of analytic sets over ATR₀ (Theorem 1). Nemoto's result, cited in the introduction, gives equivalence over ATR₀ with determinacy of games with payoff in B(Δ⁰₁, Σ⁰₂).

statement.name: Finite Σ¹₁ comprehension
statement.definition: For every Σ¹₁ formula φ and every n there is a set X ⊆ N with ∀m ≤ n (m ∈ X ↔ φ(m)).
statement.facts: Equivalent to Σ¹₁-Induction over RCA₀ (Lemma 5).

statement.name: Locally minimal bad array lemma
statement.definition: For a quasi-order (Q,≼), a well-founded relation <′ compatible with ≼ and a bad Q-array f, there is a g ≤′ f which is locally minimal bad with respect to <′.
statement.facts: Provable in Π11-CA0 (Theorem 2.17). Equivalent over RCA0 to Π11-CA0 (Theorem 6.5), hence not provable in ATR0.

statement.name: Minimal bad sequence lemma
statement.definition: For a quasi-order Q and a well-founded relation <′ compatible with it, if a bad Q-sequence exists then a Q-sequence that is minimal bad with respect to <′ exists.
statement.facts: Implies ACA0 over RCA0 (Lemma 6.3). Equivalent over RCA0 to Π11-CA0 and to the locally minimal bad array lemma (Theorem 6.5).

statement.name: Existence of leftmost paths through non-well-founded trees
statement.definition: If T is a non-well-founded tree then there is a leftmost path through T.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to Π11-CA0 and to the minimal bad sequence lemma (Theorem 6.5).

statement.name: n-weak weak König's lemma
statement.definition: WWKL for trees computable in the n-th Turing jump, as in Avigad–Dean–Rute.
statement.facts: For n≥1, [HBU ∨ n-WWKL] ↔ [WKL ∨ n-WWKL] over RCA₀^ω.

statement.name: WKL for trees with bounded prefix-free subsets
statement.definition: An infinite binary tree T ⊆ 2^{<N} has a path if there is c such that every prefix-free P ⊆ T has |P| ≤ c.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 (Proposition 3.1). It is implied by WKL(w-bd) and WKL(ext-bd).

statement.name: WKL for trees with bounded width
statement.definition: An infinite binary tree T ⊆ 2^{<N} has a path if there is c such that |T^{=n}| ≤ c for all n.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL(ext-bd) over RCA0 (Theorem 3.2). Not provable in RCA0 (Corollary 3.4 and Theorem 3.3, which shows that if IΣ02 fails there is a counterexample). It is provable in RCA0 + IΣ02 (Lemma 2.2). It is implied by IΣ02 ∨ VSMALL (Proposition 3.7). Together with 'there is a set X computing every set' it implies IΣ02 (Corollary 3.6). Strictly between RCA0 and WKL0. Whether it is strictly weaker than IΣ02 ∨ VSMALL is left open (Question 3.2).

statement.name: WKL for trees with bounded number of extendible nodes per level
statement.definition: An infinite binary tree T ⊆ 2^{<N} has a path if there is c such that for every n, the number of extendible nodes of length n is at most c.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL(w-bd) over RCA0 (Theorem 3.2). Provable from IΣ02 (Lemma 2.2). Not provable in RCA0 (Corollary 3.4).

statement.name: Σ01-WKL for bounded prefix-free subsets
statement.definition: An infinite Σ01 binary tree has a path if prefix-free subsets of the tree are bounded in size by some c.
statement.facts: Equivalent to BΣ02 and to KL(pf-bd) over RCA0 (Theorem 2.1).

statement.name: Σ01-WKL for bounded width (Chaitin's lemma)
statement.definition: An infinite Σ01 binary tree has a path if |T^{=n}| ≤ c for all n.
statement.facts: Equivalent to IΣ02 and to KL(w-bd) over RCA0 (Theorem 2.3).

statement.name: Σ01-WKL for bounded extendible nodes
statement.definition: An infinite Σ01 binary tree has a path if the number of extendible nodes of each length is bounded by some c.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 and to KL(ext-bd) over RCA0 (Corollary 1.2, using Proposition 1.1).

statement.name: König's lemma with bounded prefix-free subsets
statement.definition: An infinite tree T ⊆ N^{<N} has a path if prefix-free subsets of T are bounded in size by some c.
statement.facts: Equivalent to BΣ02 and to Σ01-WKL(pf-bd) over RCA0 (Theorem 2.1).

statement.name: König's lemma with bounded width
statement.definition: An infinite tree T ⊆ N^{<N} has a path if |T^{=n}| ≤ c for all n.
statement.facts: Equivalent to IΣ02 and to Σ01-WKL(w-bd) over RCA0 (Theorem 2.3).

statement.name: König's lemma with bounded extendible nodes
statement.definition: A finitely branching infinite tree T ⊆ N^{<N} has a path if the number of extendible nodes of each length is bounded by some c.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 and to Σ01-WKL(ext-bd) over RCA0 (Corollary 1.2).

statement.name: WKL variants producing recursive paths
statement.definition: An infinite binary tree T ⊆ 2^{<N} has a T-recursive path if the width, respectively the number of extendible nodes per level, is bounded by some c.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to IΣ02 over RCA0.

statement.name: Very smallness (Binns–Kjos-Hanssen)
statement.definition: An infinite binary tree has a path if for every function f there is n such that for all m ≥ n, the number of extendible nodes of length f(m) is below m.
statement.facts: IΣ02 ∨ VSMALL implies WKL(w-bd) over RCA0 (Proposition 3.7).

statement.name: Bounded Ramsey's theorem for triples with bound ℓ = 4 (more generally BRT^n_{2,ℓ})
statement.definition: Every coloring f : [N]^3 → 2 with no f-homogeneous set for color 1 of size 4 has an infinite f-homogeneous set for color 0. BRT^n_{2,ℓ} is the same statement for n-tuples and bound ℓ.
statement.facts: BRT^3_{2,4} is not ω-reducible to RT^2_2 with any fixed number k of applications (Theorem 1.7). It is not computably reducible to RT^2 (Theorem 1.8), and RT^2_2 ≤c BRT^3_{2,4}. It does not preserve ℓ among k hyperimmunities for suitable triangle-free graphs (Corollary 4.6). The question whether BRT^3_2 ≤ω RT^2_2 is left open.

statement.name: Taylor's Canonical Hindman's Theorem
statement.definition: For all c : N -> N there is an infinite H = {h0<h1<...} such that one of five canonical cases holds for the colour of sums over H (constant; injective in I; depends only on min(I); only on max(I); only on both min and max).
statement.facts: canHT implies HT and canHT implies λregHT (both over RCA0 and by strong Weihrauch reductions, Propositions 1 and 3). canHT implies canHT[ap] (Theorem 2).

statement.name: Regressive Hindman's Theorem
statement.definition: For every λ-regressive c : N -> N (c(n) < λ(n) if λ(n) > 0) there is an infinite H such that FS(H) is min-term-homogeneous for c.
statement.facts: Implies RT^1 (Lemma 3), HT (Proposition 5) and λregHT[ap] (Proposition 4, strongly Weihrauch). It follows from canHT (Proposition 3).

statement.name: Bounded λ-regressive Hindman's Theorems with apartness
statement.definition: λregHT restricted to sums of exactly n terms (resp. at most n terms) and with the apartness condition imposed on the solution set.
statement.facts: For n >= 2, λregHT^{=n}[ap] is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorems 3 and 4). It satisfies λregHT^{=n}[ap] ≥W RAN, ≥W WOP(X -> ω^X), ≥c HT^{=n}_k[ap] and ≥c IPT^2_2, and ≤sW regRT^n. RT^3_3 ≰c λregHT^{=2}[ap].

statement.name: Kanamori–McAloon Regressive Ramsey's Theorem
statement.definition: For every regressive c : [N]^n -> N there is an infinite min-homogeneous set.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 for n >= 2 (Theorem 1). RT^n_k ≤c regRT^n (Proposition 7). RT^{2n-1}_2 ≥sW regRT^n (Hirst). regRT^n ≰c RT^n_k (Corollary 3).

statement.name: Canonical Ramsey's Theorem (Erdős–Rado)
statement.definition: For every c : [N]^n -> N there is an infinite canonical set H and S ⊆ {1..n} such that c(I) = c(J) iff I and J agree on S.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 for n >= 2 (Theorem 1). It implies RT^n and regRT^n.

statement.name: Hindman-type theorems with apartness
statement.definition: Hindman's Theorem (possibly restricted to sums of exactly or at most n terms) with the apartness condition on the solution set.
statement.facts: HT ≥sW HT[ap] (Corollary 1). HT^{=2}_2[ap] is strictly weaker than ACA0 (follows from RT^2_2). HT^{=n}_k[ap] is equivalent to ACA0 for n >= 3, k >= 2 (cited from [5]).

statement.name: Well-ordering preservation principle for base-ω exponentiation
statement.definition: For every linear order X, if X is well-ordered then ω^X is well-ordered (an instance is an infinite descending sequence in ω^X, a solution one in X).
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 (Girard, Hirst). WOP(X -> ω^X) ≤W λregHT^{=n}[ap] for n >= 2 (Theorem 6). It is also ≤W RT^3_3 (cited from [7]) and claimed ≤W HT^{=3}_2[ap].

statement.name: Strong weak weak Kőnig's lemma
statement.loc: Section 1 (Strong weak weak Kőnig's lemma) and Section 6
statement.definition: If T ⊆ 2^{<ω} is a tree of positive measure, then there is a nonempty subtree S ⊆ T such that for every σ ∈ S, S has positive measure above σ. It corresponds to the strong continuous covering property.
statement.facts: RCA0 + WKL ⊢ SWWKL (Prop. 6.1). SWWKL implies WSWWKL; the converse is open. Over RCA0, SWWKL does not imply WKL (Prop. 6.5), via an ω-model with no set of PA degree. Both SWWKL and WSWWKL lie strictly between WKL and WWKL over RCA0. SWWKL implies that every closed set of positive measure has a perfect subset of positive measure, which strengthens Patey's result that 'every closed set of positive measure has a perfect subset' does not imply WKL.

statement.name: Weak strong weak weak Kőnig's lemma
statement.definition: If T ⊆ 2^{<ω} is a tree of positive measure, then there is a subtree S ⊆ T of positive measure with no dead ends. It corresponds to the continuous covering property.
statement.facts: RCA0 + WSWWKL ⊢ WWKL (Prop. 6.2). RCA0 + WWKL does not prove WSWWKL (Prop. 6.3), shown by an ω-model of incomplete ML-randoms. It is implied by SWWKL and therefore by WKL. Whether it implies SWWKL is open.

statement.name: Jordan decomposition on the rationals
statement.definition: Instances are continuous functions f on [0,1] of bounded variation. Solutions are Jordan decompositions (g,h) of f restricted to the rationals in [0,1].
statement.facts: JDQ is Weihrauch equivalent to AMD (Prop. 2.12). JDQ is strongly Weihrauch equivalent to JDQ2, its dyadic version (Lemma 2.16). Any oracle computing Jordan decompositions on the rationals of a suitable computable function has PA degree (Cor. 2.13). There is no uniform way to compute a DNC_k function from such decompositions (Cor. 2.14).

statement.name: Atomless martingale domination
statement.definition: Instances are lower semicontinuous presentations of atomless martingales M. Solutions are martingales majorizing M.
statement.facts: AMD is Weihrauch equivalent to JDQ (Prop. 2.12). PJDQ2 and JDQ2 are strongly Weihrauch reducible to AMD and AMD is strongly Weihrauch reducible to JDQ2 (Prop. 2.18, 2.21).

statement.name: Stable fallow Erdős–Moser theorem for finitely many colors
statement.definition: For any k and any stable k-coloring c (limy c(x,y) exists for each x), there is an infinite set A on which c is fallow, that is, c(x,z) ∈ {c(x,y), c(y,z)} for all x<y<z in A.
statement.facts: IΣ^0_2 proves the ≪2-basis theorem for sEM_{<∞} (Theorem 3.5, whose proof reduces EM_{<∞} to this case). RCA0 + IΣ^0_2 proves COH + sEM_{<∞} → EM_{<∞}.

statement.name: Σ¹₁ axiom of choice (as base theory)
statement.definition: ACA₀ plus the schema ∀n∃Xφ(n,X) → ∃Y∀nφ(n,(Y)_n) for Σ¹₁ formulas φ. This is the catalogue's sigma11ac, so it is not a new principle.
statement.facts: Used as the base theory for the incompleteness theorems. No Σ¹₁-AC₀ facts relating catalogue statements are proved. The paper shows that Π¹₁-sound Σ¹₁-definable extensions of Σ¹₁-AC₀ do not prove their own Π¹₁-soundness.

statement.name: Minimal bad sequence lemma
statement.definition: For a quasi-ordering and a well-founded relation compatible with it, every bad sequence is bounded below by a minimal bad sequence.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π¹₁-CA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.3, from Simpson–Marcone [26]).

statement.name: Locally minimal bad array lemma
statement.definition: Version of the minimal bad array lemma for arrays on barriers, with locally minimal bad arrays.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π¹₁-CA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.22, from [26]).

statement.name: Minimal bad array lemma
statement.definition: Generalization of the minimal bad sequence lemma to arrays indexed by barriers.
statement.facts: Provable in Π¹₂-CA0 by a crude analysis; its exact strength is open (Problem 2.19), conjectured not provable in Π¹₁-CA0.

statement.name: Kruskal's theorem (and generalized version)
statement.definition: Finite trees are wqo under homeomorphic embedding; generalized version for labelled trees with wqo labels.
statement.facts: Provable in Π¹₁-CA0 and not provable in ATR0 (Theorem 2.10, Friedman).

statement.name: Graph minor theorem
statement.definition: The minor ordering on finite graphs is wqo.
statement.facts: Not provable in Π¹₁-CA0 (Theorem 2.13, Friedman–Robertson–Seymour).

statement.name: Barrier theorem
statement.definition: If B is a barrier and f : B → {0,1}, then there is a subbarrier B' ⊆ B on which f is constant.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0, and to the statement that for bqo Q every map from a barrier has a perfect restriction on a subbarrier (Theorem 4.9).

statement.name: Wqo preserved by finite power set under ∃∀ ordering
statement.definition: If Q is wqo then the set of finite subsets of Q is wqo with respect to the ∃∀ quasi-ordering.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RT22.

statement.notation: closure of bqo under product, disjoint union, intersection of orderings
statement.name: Lemma 5.16 statements
statement.definition: Product of bqos is bqo; disjoint union of bqos is bqo; a bqo under two orderings is bqo under their intersection.
statement.facts: Equivalent to each other over RCA0; each implies ACA0 (Lemma 5.17) and is provable in ATR0; conjectured equivalent to ATR0 (Conjecture 5.18).

statement.name: Every wqo sequence has an increasing subsequence
statement.definition: If a quasi-ordering is wqo then every sequence has an infinite subset on which it is nondecreasing.
statement.facts: Provable in RT22 and implies RT1<∞ over RCA0; conjectured equivalent to RT22 (Conjecture 4.3).

statement.name: Cousin's lemma for Baire 2 (Baire n) functions
statement.definition: Every Baire n gauge δ : [0,1] → R+ has a δ-fine partition. Baire n+1 functions are pointwise Cauchy sequences of Baire n functions, and Baire 0 functions are the total continuous functions.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, CL_Bn implies WKL0 for every n (Theorem 7.1.6). CL_B2 implies ATR0 (Theorem 7.4.1), and implies ACA0+ (remark after Theorem 7.3.2). ACA0 does not imply CL_B2 (Theorem 7.3.2). For n ≥ 2, CL_Bn is provable in Π11-CA0 and implies ATR0 (Theorem 8.1(iii)). CL_B(n+1) implies CL_Bn since the Baire classes are nested. The strength of CL_B1 beyond implying ACA0 is open (Question 8.2).

statement.name: Sequential completeness of the reals (every Cauchy sequence in [0,1] has a limit)
statement.definition: Every Cauchy sequence of real numbers in [0,1] has a limit.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, CL_B1 implies SC (Theorem 7.2.2). SC is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (cited from Friedman 1976).

statement.name: Ginsburg–Sands theorem for CSC spaces
statement.definition: Every infinite CSC (countable second-countable, Dorais's formalization) space has an infinite subspace which is indiscrete, has the initial segment topology, has the final segment topology, is discrete, or has the cofinite topology.
statement.facts: GS is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4.6) and also equivalent to wGS. GS implies GScl, wGS and GST1.

statement.name: Weak and closure-enriched Ginsburg–Sands variants
statement.definition: wGS drops the discrete and cofinite alternatives in favour of 'T1'. GScl and wGScl are the restrictions of GS and wGS to CSC spaces for which the closure relation exists.
statement.facts: wGS is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4.6). wGScl is equivalent to CAC (Theorem 4.7). GScl is equivalent to GST1 (Theorem 4.8). The existence of the closure relation for every CSC space is equivalent to ACA0 (Proposition 4.3).

statement.name: Ginsburg–Sands theorem for T1 CSC spaces
statement.definition: Every infinite T1 CSC space has an infinite subspace which is discrete or has the cofinite topology.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, GST1 ↔ SGST1 + COH (Corollary 6.6), GST1 implies ADS (Theorem 6.5), and GST1 implies RT22 (Corollary 6.10). GST1 is strictly weaker than ACA0, since it has an ω-model without PA degrees and admits cone avoidance (Corollary 6.11). It has an ω-model consisting of low2 sets (Corollary 6.16). Every computable instance has a Δ⁰₂ discrete subspace or a computable cofinite subspace (Theorem 6.12). There is an ω-model of RT22 which is not a model of GST1 (Corollary 7.5). Whether it implies MTT22 or TT22 is open.

statement.name: Ginsburg–Sands theorem for stable T1 CSC spaces
statement.definition: The restriction of GST1 to stable CSC spaces, where a space is stable if for every x either {x} is open or every open set containing x is cofinite.
statement.facts: SGST1 + COH → GST1 (Proposition 6.4). SGST1 ↔ Σ02-Subset over RCA0 (Proposition 6.8). SGST1 implies SRT22 (Corollary 6.9).

statement.name: Σ⁰ₙ subset principle and Δ⁰ₙ subset principle
statement.definition: The scheme asserting that for every Σ⁰ₙ formula φ there is an infinite set Y equal to {x : φ(x)} or to its complement. The Δ⁰ₙ version requires φ and ψ to be Σ⁰ₙ with φ ↔ ψ.
statement.facts: Δ02-Subset is equivalent to D22 and SRT22, and Σ02-Subset is equivalent to SGST1 over RCA0. Σ02-Subset implies Δ02-Subset (hence SRT22). Every Σ⁰₂ set has an infinite low2 subset in it or its complement (Theorem 6.14). The proof of Theorem 7.1 shows there is an ω-model of RCA0 + RT22 (D22 + COH) not satisfying Σ02-Subset, and by relativization Δ0n-Subset does not imply Σ0n-Subset for n ≥ 2. Σ02-Subset does not imply Δ03-Subset. The hierarchy is summarized in Figure 2.

statement.notation: effectively discrete / effectively Hausdorff CSC space statements
statement.name: Effective discreteness statements for CSC spaces
statement.definition: Statements such as 'every discrete CSC space is effectively discrete' and 'every infinite effectively Hausdorff CSC space has an infinite effectively discrete subspace'.
statement.facts: The first is equivalent to ACA0 (Proposition 3.10). Every infinite Hausdorff CSC space has an infinite discrete subspace, provably in RCA0 (Theorem 5.2). The second statement is not provable in RCA0, since a computable counterexample exists (Theorem 5.4, Corollary 5.5); its exact strength is open (Question 8.1).

statement.name: Brouwer fixed point theorem in dimension n
statement.definition: Given a continuous f : [0,1]^n → [0,1]^n, output a fixed point.
statement.facts: BFT_n ≡_W CC_[0,1]^n ≤_W WKL, BFT_1 ≡_W IVT, and BFT_3 ≡_W WKL (cited, Fact 2.21).

statement.name: Pigeonhole principle for Σ⁰ₙ formulas
statement.definition: For every Σ⁰ₙ formula φ(x) there is an infinite set H such that either ∀x∈H φ(x) or ∀x∈H ¬φ(x).
statement.facts: Σ⁰ₙ₊₁-Subset has a weakly lowₙ basis and a lowₙ₊₁ basis (Main Theorem 1.6, Cor. 6.1, Thm 6.26). Over RCA₀, Σ⁰ₙ-Subset does not imply Δ⁰ₙ₊₁-Subset (Cor. 6.2, via ω-models). Δ⁰ₙ₊₁-Subset does not imply Σ⁰ₙ₊₁-Subset (Cor. 7.2), so the hierarchy Σ⁰₁ < Δ⁰₂ < Σ⁰₂ < Δ⁰₃ < … is strict (Main Theorem 1.9). RCA₀+IΣ⁰ₙ+Σ⁰ₙ-Subset is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀+IΣ⁰ₙ for n ≥ 2 (Main Theorem 1.10). Σ⁰₂-Subset does not preserve hyperimmunity at levels {0,1}. Whether Σ⁰₂-Subset is Π¹₁-conservative over BΣ⁰₂ is open.

statement.name: Pigeonhole principle for Δ⁰ₙ formulas
statement.definition: For Σ⁰ₙ φ and Π⁰ₙ ψ with ∀x(φ↔ψ), there is an infinite H with ∀x∈H φ(x) or ∀x∈H ¬φ(x).
statement.facts: Δ⁰ₙ₊₁-Subset has no lowₙ basis [13] and a weakly lowₙ basis [34]. It preserves hyperimmunity at levels {n−2,n−1} (Main Theorem 1.8). RCA₀+Δ⁰ₙ₊₂-Subset is not Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀+BΣ⁰ₙ₊₁ (Prop. 8.15), e.g. Δ⁰₃-Subset is not Π¹₁-conservative over BΣ⁰₂. Only Δ⁰₂-Subset was matched to catalogue entry d22; its facts are listed under d22.

statement.name: Ginsburg–Sands theorem for T1-spaces
statement.definition: Every infinite T₁ topological space has an infinite subspace homeomorphic to the discrete or the cofinite topology on N.
statement.facts: RCA₀ ⊢ GST₁ ↔ COH + Σ⁰₂-Subset (Benham et al.). GST₁ admits a weakly low basis (Cor. 6.32). RCA₀+IΣ⁰₂+GST₁ is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀+IΣ⁰₂ (Cor. 8.14).

statement.name: WWKL with measure bound q
statement.definition: Every subtree T of 2^{<ω} with |{σ ∈ 2^n : σ ∈ T}|/2^n ≥ q for all n has an infinite path.
statement.facts: RCA0 proves WWKL ↔ q-WWKL for each q (Proposition 4.4 formalized). Proposition 4.7: p-WWKL ≰W q-WWKL for rationals p<q<1. There is no effective procedure uniformly blowing up the measure and also yielding uniform reductions (Proposition 4.5).

statement.name: Thin set theorem for n-tuples and k colors
statement.definition: Every f: [N]^n → k (k ∈ {2,3,...,ω}) has an infinite thin set; the solution includes the omitted color.
statement.facts: TS^n_2 is RT^n_2. Implications go in the opposite direction to RT: TS^n_k ≤sW TS^n_j for j<k. TS^{n+2}_{2^n} implies ACA over RCA0. TS^3_8 + CAC, TS^3_7 + ADS and TS^3_6 + SHER each imply RT^2_2 over RCA0, and TS^3_3 implies RT^2_{<∞}. For every n, SeqTS^n_k has a computable instance with no ∅^(n)-computable solution but every solution computes ∅^(n). Theorem 5.27: TS^1_j ≰W TS^1_k for j<k; Theorem 5.28 (Hirschfeldt–Jockusch) extends this to n>1. Only some instances (ts23, ts24, ts2, ts13) are in the catalogue.

statement.name: Thin set theorem for singletons with infinitely many colors
statement.definition: Every f: N → ω has an infinite thin set (omitting a color).
statement.facts: Every computable instance of SeqTS^1_ω has a ∅'-computable solution (Proposition 5.22), SeqTS^1_ω ≤sW TJ^1, and every computable instance has a low2 solution (Theorem 5.24). SeqTS^1_ω ≤sW L2 (Corollary 5.26). Also a cone-avoidance statement is mentioned.

statement.name: Semi-trivial Ramsey principle
statement.definition: Every semi-trivial coloring f: [N]^2 → 2 has an infinite homogeneous set.
statement.facts: Equivalent to RT^1_{<∞} over RCA0 but apparently not strongly Weihrauch equivalent. CAC, ADS and SHER each imply it and none of these implications reverse.

statement.name: Rainbow Ramsey theorem (general exponent and bound)
statement.definition: Every k-bounded f: [ω]^n → ω has an infinite rainbow; RRT^n_{<∞} is (∀k) RRT^n_k.
statement.facts: Every computable instance of SeqRRT^1_{<∞} has a computable solution. Every computable instance of SeqRRT^2_k has a solution computable in any 2-random (Theorem 6.6). SeqRRT^2_{<∞} ≰W 2-WWKL (Corollary 6.12), and some computable instance has no solution computable from some 2-random (Proposition 6.11).

statement.name: Ramsey-type König's lemma
statement.definition: For every infinite finitely branching subtree of N^{<N}, there is an infinite homogeneous partial function.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.17). Also equivalent to ACA0 when restricted to trees with at most two successors per node.

statement.name: Ramsey-type bounded König's lemma
statement.definition: Ramsey-type König's lemma for infinite bounded subtrees of N^{<N}.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL over RCA0 (Theorem 3.19). Also WKL for trees bounded by an arbitrarily slow order function.

statement.name: Localized Ramsey-type weak König's lemma
statement.definition: For every infinite tree T ⊆ 2^{<N} and infinite X, there is an infinite H ⊆ X homogeneous for T.
statement.facts: Equivalent to RWKL over RCA0 (Lemma 3.22).

statement.name: Localized Ramsey-type weak weak König's lemma
statement.definition: RWWKL for trees of positive measure, with the homogeneous set required to be a subset of a given infinite X.
statement.facts: Equivalent to DNR and RWWKL over RCA0 (Theorem 3.24).

statement.name: Ramsey-type WKL for k-branching trees
statement.definition: RWKL (resp. LRWKL) for infinite subtrees of k^{<N}.
statement.facts: For fixed k ≥ 2 each is equivalent to RWKL over RCA0 (Theorem 3.27). ∀k RWKL_k implies RT^1 (equivalently BΣ02) over RCA0. WKL0 does not prove ∀k RWKL_k, but WKL0 + BΣ02 does.

statement.name: Localized and r.e. variants of Ramsey-type satisfiability
statement.loc: Definition 4.3 and the paragraph after it
statement.definition: Localized (infinite H ⊆ X) and r.e. (list of formulas) variants of RSAT.
statement.facts: All equivalent to RWKL and RSAT over RCA0 (Theorem 4.7).

statement.name: Localized Ramsey-type graph k-coloring
statement.definition: RCOLOR_k with the infinite homogeneous set required to be a subset of a given infinite X ⊆ V.
statement.facts: Equivalent to RWKL for k ≥ 3 (Corollary 5.14). Equivalent to RCOLOR_2 for k = 2 (Theorem 5.17).

statement.name: Ramsey-type graph k-coloring for k ≥ 4
statement.definition: For every infinite locally k-colorable graph there is an infinite k-homogeneous set.
statement.facts: Equivalent to RWKL for every standard k ≥ 3 (Corollary 5.14). Only k = 3 and k = 2 are in the catalogue.

statement.name: Packed Ramsey-type weak König's lemma
statement.definition: For every order function g with g(n) ≤ n and every infinite T ⊆ 2^{<N}, there is an infinite h homogeneous for T and packed for g.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL over RCA0.

statement.name: Homogeneous sets for color 0 for trees with no eventually-1 path
statement.definition: For every infinite tree T ⊆ 2^{<N} with no path eventually 1, there is an infinite set homogeneous for T with color 0.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL over RCA0.

statement.name: Higher relativized RWWKL and DNR
statement.definition: RWWKL for X^{(n-1)}-computable trees of positive measure, and DNR relative to X^{(n-1)}.
statement.facts: n-RWWKL → n-DNR over RCA0 + BΣ0n (Lemma 3.6). n-DNR → n-RWWKL over RCA0 + IΣ0n (Lemma 3.7). They are equivalent over RCA0 + IΣ0n (Theorem 3.8). Whether 2-RWWKL implies BΣ02 is open (Question 3.9). The n = 2 case lies in the catalogue as rwwkl2 and dnr0, but only over bases not expressible as a reduction id.

statement.name: Alternative definitions of well-quasi-order
statement.definition: wqo(set): every f:N→Q has an infinite non-decreasing subsequence set. wqo(anti): no infinite descending sequence and no infinite antichain. wqo(ext): every linear extension is a well-order.
statement.facts: Over RCA0 wqo(set) implies wqo, and wqo implies wqo(anti) and wqo(ext). No other implication holds in REC. WKL0 proves wqo(ext) implies wqo. 'Every wqo(anti) is wqo(set)' is equivalent to CAC. 'Every wqo is wqo(set)' implies RT^1_<∞. 'Every finite quasi-order is wqo(set)' is equivalent to RT^1_<∞. 'Every well-order is wqo(set)' is equivalent to ADS.

statement.name: Kruskal's tree theorem for labelled trees
statement.definition: If Q is wqo then finite trees labelled by Q, under homeomorphic embedding, are wqo.
statement.facts: Provable in Π^1_1-CA0 and in Towsner's Σ2-LPP0. Implies ATR0 (Theorem 6.12). The unlabelled statement is not provable in ATR0 (Friedman).

statement.notation: Minimal bad sequence lemma / locally minimal bad array lemma
statement.name: Minimality arguments
statement.definition: Existence of minimal bad sequences or locally minimal bad arrays for well-founded compatible relations.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to Π^1_1-CA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4.7). The minimal bad array lemma is provable in Π^1_2-CA0 and its exact strength is open.

statement.name: Robertson–Seymour theorem
statement.definition: Graph minor order on finite graphs is wqo.
statement.facts: Not provable in Π^1_1-CA0 (Friedman–Robertson–Seymour). A Π^1_1 statement, hence it holds in every ω-model.

statement.name: Laver's theorem (linear orders are bqo)
statement.definition: The countable linear orders under embeddability form a bqo.
statement.facts: Provable in Π^1_1-CA0 (Theorem 6.28). Implies ATR0 via Fraïssé's conjecture.

statement.name: Product of wqos is wqo
statement.definition: If Q1 and Q2 are wqo then Q1×Q2 is wqo.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 + CAC, implies ADS. Towsner: WKL0 does not prove it implies CAC, nor that ADS implies it.

statement.name: Young diagrams wqo
statement.definition: The Young diagrams ordered componentwise are wqo.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to ω^ω being well-ordered (Hatzikiriakou–Simpson).

statement.notation: every wqo is a finite union of ideals
statement.name: Finite ideal decomposition of wqos
statement.definition: Every wqo is a finite union of ideals.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Two-sided König duality theorem
statement.definition: Given a graph, produce an odd cycle or a König cover.
statement.facts: KDT2 ≤W LPO × KDT, and KDT ≡W KDT2 (Proposition 9.5).

statement.name: Ramsey-type cohesiveness principle
statement.definition: Every sequence of sets R_0, R_1, ... admits an infinite set C that is Ramsey-cohesive, i.e. C ⊆* R_n or C ⊆* complement of R_n for infinitely many n.
statement.facts: It is a restriction of COH and is strictly weaker. RCOH is omnisciently computably reducible to RT^1_2 (Theorem 2.5). RCOH is computably equivalent to JI∘RWKL′ (Lemma 2.10). There is an ω-model of RCOH that is not a model of COH (Theorem 2.11).

statement.name: Jump-relativized Ramsey-type weak König's lemma
statement.definition: RWKL′: for g with lim_s g(σ,s) existing for all σ and T = {σ : lim_s g(σ,s) = 1} a tree, find an infinite set homogeneous for T. JI is the jump-inversion problem, and JI∘RWKL′ asks for a limit approximation to a solution of RWKL′.
statement.facts: JI ∘ RWKL′ ≡_c RCOH (Lemma 2.10).

statement.name: Δ⁰₂ hyperimmunity
statement.definition: For every set Z and every Δ⁰₂(Z) k-partition A_0 ⊔ ... ⊔ A_{k-1} = ω, there are i < k and an infinite set X such that A_i is Z⊕X-hyperimmune within X.
statement.facts: DHYP_2 ≤_c SRT^2_2. COH ≤_c SRT^2_2 iff COH ≤_c DHYP_2 (Proposition 5.5). DHYT ≤_c DHYP_2. Whether SRT^2_2 ≤_c DHYP_2 is open (Question 5.10(3)).

statement.name: Δ⁰₂ hypertransitivity
statement.loc: Definition 5.7 and the principle following it
statement.definition: For every Z and every Δ⁰₂(Z) stable coloring c: [ω]^2 → 2 there is an infinite X such that c is Z⊕X-hypertransitive within X, i.e. the c-compatible finite sets form a Z-hyperimmune collection within X.
statement.facts: DHYT ≤_c DHYP_2 and DHYT ≤_c SEM. COH ≤_c SRT^2_2 iff COH ≤_c DHYT (Proposition 5.8). SRT^2_2 ≰_c DHYT. Question 5.10 leaves open whether SEM ≤_c DHYT and whether DHYP_2 ≤_c DHYT.

statement.name: Δ⁰₂ subset principle for 3 colors
statement.definition: Every stable c: [ω]^2 → 3 has an infinite limit-homogeneous set.
statement.facts: D^2_3 ≰_c D^2_2 (Patey [34, Corollary 3.3]), by a cardinality argument on preserving 2 among 3 hyperimmunities. D^2_3 ≤_c D^2_4. D^2_3 ≤_c D^2_2 ⋆ D^2_2 for the compositional product. Whether D^2_3 ≤_c D^2_2 × D^2_2 is open (Question 6.1).

statement.name: Dual Ramsey Theorem for Borel colorings of k-partitions with ℓ colors
statement.definition: For every Borel ℓ-coloring of the k-block partitions of ω there is an infinite partition p and a color i with all k-coarsenings of p in C_i.
statement.facts: Implies Baire-DRT over RCA0 (Prop 3.12). Baire-DRT implies it over ATR0 (Prop 3.17). For k ≥ 3 it is essentially a relativization of CDRT. Theorem 4.7: for each recursive α there is a computable Borel code for a Δ0_α coloring whose homogeneous partitions compute ∅^(α-1) (α finite) or ∅^(α) (α infinite). Theorem 5.4 gives upper bounds for k = 2. A homogeneous partition computable from the codes exists for computable open colorings (Thm 5.1), but non-uniformly (Thm 5.5).

statement.name: Dual Ramsey Theorem for Baire colorings
statement.definition: The Dual Ramsey Theorem for colorings given by a Baire code (open sets O_i and dense open sets D_n).
statement.facts: Equivalent to ODRT^k_ℓ and CDRT^k_ℓ over RCA0 (Thm 3.9). Provable in RCA0 for k = 2. Every Borel coloring has a Baire code in ATR0.

statement.name: Dual Ramsey Theorem for open colorings
statement.definition: The Dual Ramsey Theorem where each color is given by a code for an open set (Miller–Solomon).
statement.facts: Equivalent to Baire-DRT and CDRT over RCA0. ODRT^{k+1}_ℓ implies RT^k_ℓ over RCA0, so ODRT^k_ℓ implies ACA0 for k ≥ 4. ODRT^2_ℓ is provable in RCA0 (Prop 3.11).

statement.name: Combinatorial Dual Ramsey Theorem
statement.definition: For every coloring of the finite (k-1)-block partitions (ω)^{k-1}_fin with ℓ colors there is an infinite partition p and a color i such that x↾μ^x(k-1) has color i for every k-coarsening x of p.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ODRT and Baire-DRT over RCA0. CDRT^{k+1}_ℓ implies RT^k_ℓ (Cor 3.10). Provable in RCA0 for k = 2. Hindman's theorem for ℓ colors implies CDRT^3_ℓ, so ACA0+ proves CDRT^3_ℓ. Provable classically for k ≥ 3 by ω·(k-2) nested applications of the Carlson-Simpson Lemma. The number of colors does not matter (Prop 3.7).

statement.name: Dual Ramsey Theorem for reduced Σ^0_n Borel colorings, k = 2
statement.definition: For each reduced coloring (ω)^2 = R0 ∪ R1 with R0, R1 Borel codes for Σ^0_n sets, there are an infinite partition x and i < 2 with (x)^2 ⊆ R_i.
statement.facts: Theorem 5.7: strongly Weihrauch equivalent to D^n_2 (every stable coloring of n-tuples has an infinite limit-homogeneous set), and equivalent to D^n_2 over RCA0 + IΣ^0_{n-1}. Hence Δ^0_2-rDRT^2_2 is equivalent to SRT^2_2 over RCA0, and Δ^0_2-rDRT^2_2 <sW SRT^2_2 (Cor 5.8, 5.9).

statement.name: Δ^0_n subset principle for stable colorings of n-tuples (2 colors)
statement.definition: Every stable coloring c: [ω]^n → 2 has an infinite limit-homogeneous set.
statement.facts: For n = 2 it is the catalogue's D^2_2. Equivalent to Δ^0_n-rDRT^2_2 under ≡sW, and over RCA0 + IΣ^0_{n-1}.

statement.name: Carlson-Simpson Lemma
statement.definition: For every coloring of (ω)^m_fin with ℓ colors there is an infinite partition p and a color i such that x↾μ^x(m) has color i for every x ∈ (p)^{m+1} that keeps the first m blocks of p distinct.
statement.facts: Special case of CDRT^{m+1}_ℓ (Prop 3.26). Equivalent to the stronger versions in Prop 3.27. CDRT^k_ℓ follows from transfinitely many applications of CSL. CSL(2,ℓ) follows from Hindman's theorem. It is an open question whether CSL(2,2) is computably true.

statement.name: Variable word principle
statement.definition: Variant of the Carlson-Simpson Lemma for variable words.
statement.facts: COH does not imply VW(2,2) (Erhard). WKL0 does not imply VW(2,2) (Miller–Solomon).

statement.name: Carlson-Simpson Lemma, one-dimensional version for ℓ colors
statement.definition: Weakening of OVW in which variable kinds may be interleaved and occur infinitely often; the one-dimensional version for ℓ colors generalizes TT^2_ℓ.
statement.facts: RCA0 + CSL^1_2 is ∀Π04-conservative over RCA0 + BΣ02 (Le Houérou and Patey [18]). Question 4.1 asks whether it is Π11-conservative over RCA0 + BΣ02.

statement.name: Carlson-Simpson Lemma, zero-dimensional version
statement.definition: Zero-dimensional version of the Carlson-Simpson Lemma.
statement.facts: It is an immediate consequence of OVW_0, hence Π11-conservative over RCA0 + BΣ02.

statement.name: Totality of Ackermann's function principle
statement.definition: Principle equivalent to the totality of Ackermann's function (Kreuzer and Yokoyama).
statement.facts: RCA0 + TT^1 + PΣ^0_1 is Π11-conservative over RCA0 + BΣ^0_2 + PΣ^0_1 (Chong, Li, Wang, Yang).

statement.name: Dilworth's theorem for partial orders of finite width
statement.definition: For every partial order P of finite width there is a coloring g : N → w(P) such that each g^{-1}(i) is a P-chain.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL over RCA0 (Hirst, Proposition 2.2), even restricted to width 2.

statement.name: Mirsky's theorem for partial orders of finite height
statement.definition: For every partial order P of finite height there is a coloring g : N → h(P) such that each g^{-1}(i) is a P-antichain.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL over RCA0 (Hirst, Proposition 2.7), even restricted to height 2.

statement.name: Weak Dilworth's theorem
statement.definition: For every partial order P of finite width there are k and a coloring g : N → k such that each g^{-1}(i) is a P-chain.
statement.facts: Computably true (Kierstead, Theorem 2.3); provable over RCA0 (Fiori-Carones et al., Proposition 2.4).

statement.name: Weak Mirsky's theorem
statement.definition: For every partial order P of finite height there are k and a coloring g : N → k such that each g^{-1}(i) is a P-antichain.
statement.facts: Provable over RCA0 (Proposition 2.8).

statement.name: (Iterated) Finite Union Theorem
statement.definition: Every finite (resp. sequence of finite) colorings of [M]^<ω has an infinite block sequence whose finite unions are monochromatic (for each n, FU of the tail from n is monochromatic for f_n in the iterated version).
statement.facts: Proposition 2.13: over RCA0, IFU is equivalent to IHT and IGG, and FU is equivalent to HT and GG, with restrictions to n colors.

statement.name: (Iterated) Galvin–Glazer Theorem
statement.definition: For a directed partial semigroup with no idempotents or left-cancelative, every finite coloring (resp. sequence of finite colorings) has a homogeneous infinite basic sequence.
statement.facts: Proposition 2.13: over RCA0, GG is equivalent to HT and FU, and IGG is equivalent to IHT and IFU.

statement.name: Milliken–Taylor theorem
statement.definition: For k, r, any r-coloring of [N]^k has an increasing sequence <x_i> such that all k-tuples of block-sums from consecutive blocks of FS(<x_m>) have the same color.
statement.facts: Provable in ACA0^IU for each standard k; MT(3) implies IHT (Hirst); ∀k MT(k) implies ∀k,r RT^k_r. It is provable in ACA0+ (via IHT). ∀k MT(k) is provable in (ACA0+)' and, if ACA0 proves IHT, is equivalent to ACA0' over RCA0 (Theorem 4.16).

statement.name: Ramsey-type statement with at most d colors in the output
statement.definition: Every coloring f : [ω]^n → ℓ has an infinite set H on which f uses at most d colors. TS^n_ℓ is the case d = ℓ − 1.
statement.facts: Only used to frame the thin set analysis, with no result proved about it directly.

statement.name: Stable thin set theorem for pairs with 2 colors
statement.definition: Every stable coloring f : [ω]^2 → 2 has an infinite thin set. It is the instance k=2 of STS^2_k.
statement.facts: STS^2_2 ≰_c STS^2_ℓ for ℓ > 2 (Corollary 4.10). STS^2_2 ≰_c TS^2_3 (Corollary 4.17). The conjunction Φ with TS^2_3 does not imply STS^2_2 over RCA0 (Theorems 4.14, 4.23, 4.29).

statement.name: Thin set theorem for singletons with k colors
statement.definition: Every coloring f : ω → k has an infinite set H with |f(H)| ≤ k−1. The catalogue contains only the case k=3.
statement.facts: TS^1_k ≰_sc TS^1_ℓ whenever ℓ > k ≥ 2 (Corollary 4.9). TS^1_{k+1} admits strong preservation of k non-c.e. definitions (Theorem 4.8), while TS^1_k does not.

statement.name: Thin set theorem for n-tuples with ℓ colors
statement.definition: Every coloring f : [ω]^n → ℓ has an infinite set H with |f([H]^n)| ≤ ℓ−1.
statement.facts: For every k and n, TS^n_ℓ admits strong preservation of k non-c.e. definitions for sufficiently large ℓ (Theorem 4.21).

statement.name: Countable Banach's theorem (unbounded)
statement.definition: For injections f, g : N → N there is a bijection h : N → N such that h(n) = m implies f(n) = m or g(m) = n.
statement.facts: Cited from Hirst [7, Theorem 4.1]: equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: LLPO with parity of the first zero
statement.definition: Realizer returning the parity of the first position where the sequence is zero, if there is a zero.
statement.facts: Proposition 4.1: strongly Weihrauch equivalent to LLPO, provably in RCAω0.
